source: Author requested ten additional metal salvage items, including rusted iron and machine parts, at T0 and T1 with varying rarities, October 16, 2026. Local catalog proposals under Docs/WORLD_BASIS.md.
scope: Append ten Salvage definitions only: six T0 and four T1. Rarity is independent of practical-worth tier. Existing items, manual edits and review/artwork state are retained. Deterministic world identity, streaming and unload/reload, generated-object identity, authored placement constraints and persisted runtime deltas are not applicable: this batch adds catalog definitions without spawning objects or changing runtime, placement, recipes or saved games.

defaults.Carrier metadata: Recovered metal cargo; dimensions, carrying mass and packing remain undefined.
defaults.Acquisition: Recover from discarded contemporary workshop fittings, frames or machinery. Exact sites, encounter frequency and collection requirements remain design work.
defaults.Crafting / processing: Inspect, clean and sort the recovered piece before assessing surviving metal or possible donor use. No recovery quantity, repair recipe or working replacement part is established.
defaults.Limitations: As-found salvage with uncertain integrity. No qualified replacement fit, load rating, crafting readiness, guaranteed metal yield or automatic processing result.
defaults.Classification basis: Contemporary recovered metal pieces, cataloged as salvage for condition assessment and possible material or donor-part recovery.

items.name: Flaking iron bolt stubs
items.purpose: A few snapped iron bolt shanks with missing heads and thick rust scales filling the remaining threads. Their short, uneven cores offer little donor-part utility, but can be sorted as small ferrous scrap after inspection.
items.icon: Three short irregular rust-red iron bolt stubs with broken ends, missing heads and flaking thread ridges; no complete fasteners or tools.

fields.Search aliases: rusted iron; broken bolt shanks; snapped fasteners; ferrous scrap
fields.Tier basis: T0: short fractured shanks with little surviving useful geometry and modest recoverable metal.
fields.Open design decisions: Junk rarity: routine fastener debris. Resolve corrosion loss, recoverable quantity and sorting route; no usable bolt or threading is granted.

items.name: Crushed iron conduit elbow
items.purpose: A rusted right-angle iron conduit fitting flattened across its bend. Both sockets are distorted and packed with grit, leaving a recognizable hollow fitting suitable mainly for metal recovery rather than carrying a line or protecting a cable.
items.icon: One small rusted iron ninety-degree conduit elbow with a crushed bend, distorted sockets and packed sand; no cable or long pipe section.

fields.Search aliases: rusted elbow; crushed conduit fitting; iron socket scrap; bent pipe fitting
fields.Tier basis: T0: crushed hollow section and ruined sockets eliminate most fitting utility.
fields.Open design decisions: Junk rarity: ordinary discarded conduit debris. Resolve wall thickness, contamination and recovery route; no usable conduit or electrical protection rating.

items.name: Broken cast-iron mounting foot
items.purpose: A squat cast-iron machine foot broken through its mounting hole. A missing corner and granular fracture face leave too little sound shape to secure equipment, though the heavy fragment remains a candidate for sorted iron feed.
items.icon: One squat dark rusted cast-iron mounting foot with a broken bolt hole, missing corner and coarse fracture face; no attached machine or intact bracket.

fields.Search aliases: cast iron scrap; broken machine foot; cracked mounting lug; rusted iron fragment
fields.Tier basis: T0: brittle fracture through the fixing point prevents useful mounting; bulk alone does not establish high-value stock.
fields.Open design decisions: Junk rarity: ordinary broken cast hardware. Resolve mass, hidden cracking and material recovery; no sound mount or structural reuse implied.

items.name: Rusted square washer stack
items.purpose: Several square iron washers stuck together by rust, with rounded corners and enlarged central holes. Separating them may expose a few small packing blanks, but their worn faces and uncertain thickness keep them in the low-value scrap band.
items.icon: A short uneven stack of four square iron washers fused with orange rust, rounded corners and enlarged holes; no nuts or bolts.

fields.Search aliases: square washers; rusted washer pile; iron packing scrap; fused washers
fields.Tier basis: T0: small worn pieces and uncertain separation leave little assured repair utility.
fields.Open design decisions: Common rarity: recognizable square hardware occurs less often than mixed fragments but remains an ordinary find. Assess separability and usable faces; no guaranteed washer count or load-bearing use.

items.name: Seized iron oil-cup cap
items.purpose: A tiny threaded iron cap recovered with the broken neck of a machine oil cup seized inside it. Its narrow knurled rim is recognizable, but corrosion has blocked the thread and the attached fragment prevents treating it as a usable closure.
items.icon: One tiny rusty knurled iron oil-cup cap with a jagged broken neck seized in its threads; dry, without oil or a complete vessel.

fields.Search aliases: oil cup lid; rusted lubricator cap; seized threaded cap; dry machinery scrap
fields.Tier basis: T0: very little metal, blocked threads and a trapped fragment provide almost no assured donor utility.
fields.Open design decisions: Uncommon rarity: this small recognizable service fitting is less frequently recovered intact enough to identify. Resolve material and separability; it contains no usable lubricant or restored seal.

items.name: Broken fine-pitch gauge leaf
items.purpose: A thin iron-alloy leaf from a specialist thread gauge, snapped across its toothed edge and freckled with rust. A few closely spaced teeth and a worn pitch marking remain, identifying an unusual workshop find whose missing reference edge prevents reliable measurement.
items.icon: One thin rust-spotted metal gauge leaf with a broken fine-toothed edge, a small pivot hole and faint pitch marks; no complete gauge set.

fields.Search aliases: thread pitch gauge scrap; broken gauge blade; fine toothed measuring leaf; rusty workshop gauge
fields.Tier basis: T0: tiny metal quantity and a destroyed measuring edge leave negligible assured practical utility.
fields.Open design decisions: Rare rarity: a recognizable specialist fine-pitch gauge fragment is an unusual find; rarity does not restore its accuracy or raise scrap value. Resolve original pitch and alloy; no calibrated measurement, ancient provenance or collector premium is established.

items.name: Rusted iron U-bolt clamp
items.purpose: A U-shaped iron clamp recovered with its crossbar and one stubborn nut. Rust covers the curve and the exposed threads are bruised, but the broad shape and surviving clamp hardware offer a modest donor candidate after cleaning and inspection.
items.icon: One rusted iron U-bolt with a flat crossbar, one retained nut and one bare threaded end; no pipe, cable or surrounding frame.

fields.Search aliases: u bolt clamp; rusty pipe saddle clamp; recovered iron fastener; threaded clamp
fields.Tier basis: T1: a substantial surviving clamp shape and retained crossbar offer more potential reuse than fractured or crushed fragments.
fields.Open design decisions: Common rarity: ordinary frame and pipe hardware. Assess thread damage, metal loss, span and fatigue; no safe clamping load or working replacement is granted.

items.name: Pitted iron spacer sleeve
items.purpose: A short thick-walled iron spacer with rust pits along its outer surface and wear on both end faces. Its open central bore and substantial ring section survive, offering a possible donor blank or packing spacer once its dimensions and remaining metal have been checked.
items.icon: One short thick-walled rusty iron spacer sleeve with an open central bore, pitted outside and worn flat ends; no shaft or bearing assembly.

fields.Search aliases: iron spacer tube; pitted distance sleeve; thick metal spacer; rusty ring blank
fields.Tier basis: T1: a largely continuous thick section retains ordinary donor geometry and useful metal despite worn faces.
fields.Open design decisions: Common rarity: standard machinery spacing hardware. Resolve bore, length, wall loss and end-face condition; no bearing fit or precision alignment is implied.

items.name: Seized bronze flanged bushing
items.purpose: A bronze sleeve bushing with a green-brown patina, a worn flange and a scored bore holding a short rusted iron shaft stub. Its recoverable bronze and surviving worked section make a modestly useful find, while the seized mixed-metal core prevents immediate bearing reuse.
items.icon: One patinated bronze flanged bushing with a scored bore and short rusty iron stub seized inside; no complete bearing, lubricant or surrounding housing.

fields.Search aliases: bronze bush; flanged bronze sleeve; seized bearing bush; mixed metal scrap
fields.Tier basis: T1: nonferrous recovery potential and a surviving flange give modest worth, reduced by seizure, scoring and separation work.
fields.Open design decisions: Uncommon rarity: a recognizable bronze donor is less routine than ferrous scrap. Resolve alloy, shaft separation, recoverable quantity and bore wear; no usable bearing surface or guaranteed bronze yield.

items.name: Left-thread iron turnbuckle barrel
items.purpose: A rusted iron tensioning barrel with one left-hand and one right-hand threaded socket. Both matching end rods are missing. The central body retains useful worked metal and unusual opposing threads, but practical reuse depends on compatible fittings and condition checks.
items.icon: One short rusty iron turnbuckle barrel with opposing threaded end sockets and a central adjustment opening; no hooks, end rods, cable or complete tensioner.

fields.Search aliases: reverse thread tensioner; left hand threaded barrel; rusty turnbuckle body; opposing thread fitting
fields.Tier basis: T1: surviving worked threads offer limited donor utility, constrained by small size, corrosion and missing matched rods.
fields.Open design decisions: Rare rarity: this particular opposing-thread fitting is an unusual salvage find. Resolve thread pitch, internal corrosion and compatible ends; no universal fitting compatibility or safe tensioning load is established.
